soundness_flags.label: ass:poisson-cpcm-family
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited CPCM condition permits arbitrary source-node laws and places parametric kernels on non-source nodes; requiring Poisson kernels for every node, including roots, is a stricter Poisson-DAG subclass and should not be tagged as the cited standard CPCM condition.

soundness_flags.label: def:certificate-input and def:admissible-design-class
soundness_flags.one_line: The certificate permits any positive rational rho, but a row-allocation vector used as limits n_Sj/N_S must lie in the probability simplex; without sum_j rho_j=1, some admitted certificate inputs cannot arise from the stated sampling model.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 4 and 9--10, Definition 1, Definition 9, Definition 10, and Lemma 11.
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Definition 9 sets source nodes equal to exogenous variables, assigns the CPCM conditional family only to non-source nodes, and requires nonconstant parent effects; Definition 10 and Lemma 11 give pairwise-identifiable multivariate DAG identification from the joint law.

Theorem 12 states that the direct observational distribution identifies the PT-SEM DAG, thinning matrix, and node-wise exogenous distributions; the paper also describes a plug-in-moment BIC DAG-selection procedure with a consistency claim.

Theorem 4.3 characterizes functional-form consistency under linear aggregation; Corollary 4.4 forces affine ANM mechanisms and Corollary 4.5 forces affine PNL components under nondegenerate linear aggregation.
The paper defines Taylor models with rigorous remainder intervals and applies them to branch-and-bound rigorous global search.
The paper designs network-tomography probe allocations using A- and D-optimal Fisher-information objectives, including explicit cases and an iterative allocation algorithm.

Require rho in the rational simplex in both certificate-input and admissible-design-class, and make the certificate reject non-simplex allocations before computing covariance or required wells.
